claims.claim: Athanasius was the Patriarch of Alexandria, also called archbishop of Alexandria.
Athanasius was born c. 296–298 at Alexandria and died on 2 May 373.
The Letter to Adelphius was written in 370 or 371.
The letter was written in answer to a report which Adelphius had sent to Athanasius about the Arian charge of creature-worship brought against the Christology of Nicaea.
Adelphius was bishop of Onuphis and had previously been exiled by the Arians to the Thebaid, hence he is styled 'Confessor' in the title of the letter.
The letter is directed against the Arian Christology.
Athanasius traces the Arian error back to the Valentinians, Marcionists and Manichaeans.
Athanasius points out that Catholics do not worship the human nature of Christ as such, but the Word Incarnate.
The letter survives as part of Athanasius's collected letters, numbered as Letter 60 or Letter LX in various collections.
The Greek text of the letter survives, with the title identifying Athanasius as 'archiepiskopou Alexandreias' (archbishop of Alexandria).
The letter's style closely resembles that of the writings of Athanasius's 'third Exile.'
The date proposed by Montfaucon is adopted for the letter, though there is nothing to fix it absolutely.
